title: Design an Assistive Navigation mode for compact tables and chart annotations: keyboard map, focus memory, and VPAT evidence
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Dense data views (compact tables + small-chart annotation workflows) are frequently used in product dashboards. Users relying on keyboard-only navigation and assistive tech report: (1) discovery issues — keyboard shortcuts and actions are not discoverable, (2) focus loss when interacting with inline editors/annotations, and (3) inconsistent ARIA labeling for chart controls. This task designs a toggleable 'Assistive Navigation' mode to surface a lightweight keyboard map, persist focus across route changes, normalize ARIA on annotation controls, and produce a VPAT-ready evidence pack.
background: Over the last 18 months we've had multiple accessibility bugs and feature requests tied to dense controls: modal/tooltips stealing focus, table-row editing losing context, and chart annotation controls lacking accessible names. Several recent support tickets and audit notes (see confluence link below) requested a unified entry point for keyboard-first flows. Existing design tokens for focus and contrast were updated across components but there is no coordinated pattern for discoverability or focus memory.
goals: Provide a discoverable toggle for 'Assistive Navigation' that surfaces keyboard map and hotkeys for the current view
Ensure focus persistence when moving between table rows and associated chart annotation editors
Standardize ARIA names/roles for inline annotation tools and non-interactive chart elements
Ship a VPAT evidence pack: test matrix, screenshots, recorded keyboard walkthroughs, and remediation notes
Minimize visual noise for non-assistive users and use existing tokens for contrast/focus
scope: Compact/dense data table variant (compact density rows) and inline row editor flows
Charts that support annotations (point labels, freeform comment boxes) and tooltip controls
Design tokens and focus outline recommendations for high-contrast and theming modes
Deliverables: design specs, accessibility checklist, annotated component tokens, and VPAT evidence pack
out_of_scope: Full rebuild of data-grid into a new component (we will use current grid API)
End-to-end automation of keyboard tests (QA will provide manual recordings and guidance)
Accessibility updates for unrelated components (buttons outside dense flows)
proposed_solution: Introduce an 'Assistive Navigation' mode toggle in the top-right of dense views (persistent per-user preference). When enabled: (a) show a collapsible overlay with the current view's keyboard map (contextual hotkeys), (b) enable focus-memory for last-edited row/annotation using a lightweight focus token persisted in route state, (c) add explicit aria-labels and aria-controls for chart annotation buttons and ensure role mapping for non-interactive SVG elements, (d) enforce focus-visible styles via design tokens and fallback high-contrast values for the theme. Detailed pattern: overlay uses role='dialog' with aria-modal='false' so it doesn't trap assistive tech; hotkey map uses a semantic list and links to the first interactive element; focus-memory implemented by storing element-id in session storage and restoring focus after navigation or modal close. The design will reference current tokens for focus/outline to avoid token churn. We will produce VPAT evidence by running manual checks against WCAG 2.1 AA and assembling screenshots, narrated recordings, and a remediation log.
tasks: Design - wireframes for overlay + compact table focus state (Figma)
Spec - ARIA pattern for chart annotation controls and non-interactive SVG labeling
Tokens - document focus-outline and high-contrast fallback recommendations
Engineering - prototype focus-memory micro-library and overlay toggle
Engineering - add aria attributes to annotation controls and ensure keyboard activation order
QA - manual keyboard walkthroughs recorded, create VPAT evidence pack
Docs - update pattern library page and onboarding notes for Assistive Navigation mode
Rollout - feature flag gated release and opt-in default for existing customers
dev_notes: Prototype focus-memory using sessionStorage key 'assistive.lastFocus' and expose restoreFocus(elementId)
Use aria-describedby for tooltip relationships rather than title attributes for better screen reader support
Chart SVGs: ensure each interactive overlay has a focusable <button> with aria-label; non-interactive shapes get aria-hidden='true'
Avoid JS focus traps — overlay should not prevent shifting to other parts of the app unless explicitly requested
Add unit tests for keyboard order and e2e manual checklist for VPAT (QA will record manual runs)
acceptance_criteria: Assistive Navigation toggle exists in dense views and is persisted per user (preference key)
Keyboard map overlay is reachable via keyboard and screen reader announces the overlay succinctly
Editing a table row and opening its chart annotation editor restores focus to the editor after navigation
Chart annotation controls expose aria-label and keyboard activation order matches visual order
Design tokens for focus and contrast used in overlay and controls referenced in spec and implemented by eng
VPAT evidence pack submitted: test matrix (WCAG 2.1 AA), screenshots, 3 narrated keyboard walkthrough videos, and remediation log
qa_steps: Enable Assistive Navigation toggle, tab through to open overlay, verify screen reader announces overlay title
Navigate a compact table via keyboard to an inline row editor, edit/save, navigate to chart, open annotation editor and verify focus returns to editor
Test keyboard-only activation for chart annotation buttons in Chrome + NVDA and Safari + VoiceOver
Switch theme to high-contrast and verify focus outlines meet token-defined contrast thresholds
Run VPAT checklist: document pass/fail per criterion and attach required artifacts to ticket
